choices: you were into science fiction
you were intrigued by science fiction
you were fascinated by science fiction

solution: 밑줄 친 (A)는 ‘네가 공상 과학 소설에 관심이 있었는지’의 의 미로, ‘be동사+interested in ~'는 ’~에 관심이 있다‘는 뜻을 가 지며 어떤 것에 대한 흥미나 관심이 있음을 나타낼 때 사용된 다. 그러나 ❺ ’너는 공상 과학 소설에 대해 걱정했는지‘의 의 미이므로 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 참고로, 흥미, 관심을 나타내는 표현으로 ’be동사+into ~(~에 푹 빠지다), be동사+fascinated by ~(~에 매료되다), be동사 +curious about ~(~에 호기심이 있다), be동사+intrigued by ~(~에 강한 흥미를 느꼈다) 등이 있다.

The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from
my hometown, Waituhi. “Can you take a week off?”
he asked. “Your Nani Tama wants you here.” “But
Dad!” I answered. “My boss won’t let me take any
more time off.” The phone went silent, and then I
heard my grandfather say faintly, “I need your help,
Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the
whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have
much time.” I just knew I had no choice. “All right,
Nani,” I replied with a sigh. “I’ll come.”

윗글의 바로 뒤에 이어질 내용으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: a journey to complete whakapapa with Nani
effort to discourage Nani from continuing hiswork
unexpected changes in Waituhi due to a naturaldisaster
difficulties with persuading dad and grandfatherto go to Murupara
a reunion with people of Waituhi to celebrategrandfather’s recovery
solution: 일주일 휴가를 요청하는 아버지와 나니(=할아버지)의 요청에 거절 의 의사를 표했지만 와카파파를 마무리하기 위해 Murupara로 가야한다는 나니의 간곡한 부탁에 결국 승낙하였으므로 바로 뒤에 와카파파를 마무리하기 위한 나니와의 여정에 대한 내용 이 오는 것이 알맞다. 따라서 뒤에 이어질 내용으로 ❶ ‘나니와 함께 와카파파를 완성하는 여정’이 가장 적절하다. ② 나니가 일을 계속하지 못하게 막으려는 노력 ③ 자연재해로 인한 와이투이에서 발생한 예상치 못한 변화 ④ 아버지와 할아버지를 무루파라로 가도록 설득하는 것의 어려움 ⑤ 할아버지의 회복을 축하하기 위해 와이투이 사람들과의 재회 미래엔(김성연) 2과

body:
For some time, my grandfather had been busy
writing down the village genealogy, known as the
whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old
house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran
through the house and destroyed our past. In only
one night, everything we knew was gone. (A) Nani
Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my
Auntie Hiraina. (B) He chanted the names of the
ancestors, joining the past to the present once more.
(C) The village went quiet and listened to his chanting.
(D) His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy,
searching back across the centuries. (E) Sometimes,
there were lines that were difficult to remember. Then
his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant.
The village waited in worried silence until the next
name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama
almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa,
but there were still missing names he needed to fill in.
Now, he wanted me to drive him to Murupara to
finish his work.
Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called
Murupara. “Where do we go now?” I asked Nani. He
did not reply, but he was searching inside himself,
staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner,
he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw
an old man standing in front of a house. He
welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his
eyes, I saw the message, “We must hurry.”
Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember
the two old men sitting at the table and the soft
sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through
the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled
missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were
other people in the room. I felt ⓐ마치 과거의 사람들
이 그 작업이 정확한지를 확인하기 위해 두 노인의 어깨
너머로 보고 있는 것처럼. Finally, they stopped. It was
done. After a moment of silence, the old man
whispered to Nani, “Goodbye, friend.” Crying, they
pressed their noses together to say goodbye.
It was early morning and still dark when we
returned to Auntie’s place. All the lights were on,
and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling,
Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it
to the village. Our hearts were full because
ⓑ____________________________________________________.
Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired.
He sighed. “At last, I may go now.” Then, he closed
his eyes. “No, Dad!” Auntie Hiraina cried. The sun
burst across the hills.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: It took nearly two years for Nani to collect themajority of the whakapapa.
Nani got to Murupara shortly before noon.
Nani told the narrator the way to the house infront of which an old man was standing.
Nani and the old man spoke Maori words in softvoices while recalling missing names.
Nani and the old man pressed their noses togetherto greet each other.
solution: 두 노인이 작별 인사를 하면서 서로의 코를 맞대었다고 했으 므로 ❺ ‘나니와 노인은 서로를 맞이하기 위해 코를 맞대었다.’ 는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.

body:
Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,
which has been a culturally significant practice of
the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s
journey from their past to their present. Each
curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a
person’s whakapapa(genealogy), social positions, and
personal accomplishments. This explains why no two
tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the
Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire
faces, while women have it on their lips and chins.
The Maori start getting these designs in their
teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines
and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect
their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held
great importance as a rite of passage throughout
their lives. Although tā moko is less common these
days, it is still practiced today by Maori people,
who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage
for the next generation.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: More Than a Tattoo, Tā moko
Cultural Significance of Tattoos
The New Way of Decorating Faces
Tradition and Heritage of Tattooing
Tā moko: A Reflection of Ancestors’ Lives
solution: 마오리족의 전통적인 문신 문화인 타 모코에 관한 내용으로, 타 모코가 무엇인지, 어떤 의미를 갖는지, 왜 동일한 타 모코 가 있을 수 없는지, 문신의 위치와 나이가 들수록 늘어나는 이 유 등을 설명하는 글로, 타 모코는 단순한 문신이 아니라 개인 의 삶의 여정을 표현하는 관습이므로 글의 제목으로 ❶ ’문신 그 이상인, 타 모코’가 가장 알맞다.

When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was (A)[shocking
/ shocked] to see how thin Nani Tama was. “Look,
Nani,” I said. “I’m not taking you anywhere. You
could die on me!” Nani looked at me in anger.
“You want me to die here in this room? Looking at
these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet
finished?” The old man held on tightly to the side
of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every
slow, painful (B)[step / steps] hurt him, but he tried
to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car,
and we set off with Auntie. We traveled all night,
mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the
darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear him.
Sometimes, he burst into a song (C)[that / what] he
had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up
their voices to send the song flying like a bird
through the sky.

G: Hi, Steve. Did you do anything interesting
yesterday?
B:
Yes, I went to Cafe Grande with a few friends
and saw something pretty cool there.
G: Really? The last time I went there, I didn’t notice
anything special.
B:
Well, my drink had a big ice ball in it. I wonder
why people use such a huge, sphere-shaped
piece of ice.
G: That’s a good question. As far as I know, it can
keep the drink cool for a longer time because
that shape lasts longer than other shapes.
B:
Come to think of it, the ice in my drink melted
much slower than regular ice cubes.
G: That’s because a sphere has the least surface
area for a given volume.
B:
You mean because it has less surface area,
sphere-shaped ice melts more slowly?
G: Exactly!

The boy saw a big ice ball in his drink at thecafe.
Sphere-shaped ice helps maintain the drink'stemperature for a longer period.

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

Sound is produced through vibrations that occur
from a sound source, when the strings of a guitar
are played, for instance. The vibrations of the sound
source cause the air to vibrate and the sound to
travel as waves, similar to the ripples created in a
lake when you throw a stone.
(A) There are two types of interference: constructive
and destructive. Constructive interference occurs
when the peaks of two waves overlap, resulting
in a bigger wave and a louder sound.
(B) When these sound waves reach our ears, the
brain interprets them as sound. Just as different
ripples in water might overlap if you throw two
stones, sound waves can also interfere with each
other when they meet.
(C) Destructive interference, on the other hand,
occurs when a peak of one wave overlaps with
a valley of another wave, so they cancel each
other out and produce a quieter sound, or no
sound at all.

body:
Have you ever wondered what ⓐis happened to
sound waves when they enter our ears? Let’s take a
closer look. The journey starts from the external
part of the outer ear, which gathers the waves and
ⓑdirect them into the ear. The collected waves
then travel through the ear canal and reach the
eardrum located in the middle ear. When the
eardrum vibrates, these vibrations are transmitted to
three small bones in the middle ear. These bones
make the vibrations ⓒstronger and then pass them
to a snail-shaped structure in the inner ear. Inside
this fluid-filled structure ⓓis tiny hair cells. When
the vibrations make waves in the fluid, the tiny hair
cells move and generate electrical signals ⓔthat
travel to the auditory nerve. This nerve carries the
information to the brain, where the signals are
interpreted,
ⓕallowing
us
to
hear
sound.
Undoubtedly, it is a quite remarkable journey!

sounds from the outside, and the circuitry analyzes
them to produce opposite sound waves. For
example, if outside noise has a value of +1, the
circuitry will generate an opposite noise of –1 and
transmit it to the speakers. This cancels out the
unwanted sound even in noisy surroundings, so you
can hear the music sound clearly without turning
up the volume. (A)______________, it is not easy ⓑto
entirely eliminate external noise with this technology.

convert the noise into digital data and instantly
ⓒtransmit the opposite sound to the speakers as
soon
as

reaches

microphones.

effective for predictable sounds like ⓓthose of car

Sound (A)[produces / is produced] through vibrations
that occur from a sound source, when the strings
of a guitar are played, for instance. The vibrations
of the sound source (B)[cause / causes] the air to
vibrate and the sound to travel as waves, similar to
the ripples created in a lake when you throw a
stone. When these sound waves reach our ears, the
brain interprets them as sound. Just as different
ripples in water might overlap if you throw two
stones, sound waves can also interfere with each
other when they meet. There are two types of
interference: constructive and destructive. Constructive
interference occurs when the peaks of two waves
overlap, (C)[resulted / resulting] in a bigger wave
and a louder sound. Destructive interference, on the
other hand, occurs when a peak of one wave
overlaps with a valley of another wave, so they
cancel each other out and produce a quieter sound,
or no sound at all.

Destructive

headphones
are
microphones

noise-cancelling
circuitry.
The
microphones pick up sounds from the outside, and
the circuitry analyzes them to produce opposite
sound waves. For example, if outside noise has a
value of +1, the circuitry will generate an opposite
noise of –1 and transmit it to the speakers. This
cancels out the unwanted sound even in noisy
surroundings, so you can hear the music sound
clearly without turning up the volume. However, it
is not easy to entirely eliminate external noise with
this technology. To achieve full noise cancellation,
the circuitry must convert the noise into digital data
and instantly transmit the opposite sound to the
speakers
as

noise
reaches

microphones.

this
noise-cancellation
technology is effective for predictable sounds like
those of car engines and subways that occur
regularly or over a period of time. 그러나 그것은 당

Have you ever wondered what happens to sound
waves when they enter our ears?
(A) When the eardrum vibrates, these vibrations are
transmitted to three small bones in the middle
ear. These bones make the vibrations stronger
and then pass them to a snail-shaped structure
in the inner ear. Inside this fluid-filled structure
are tiny hair cells.
(B) When the vibrations make waves in the fluid,
the tiny hair cells move and generate electrical
signals that travel to the auditory nerve. This
nerve carries the information to the brain, where
the signals are interpreted, allowing us to hear
sound. Undoubtedly, it is a quite remarkable
journey!
(C) Let’s take a closer look. The journey starts from
the external part of the outer ear, which gathers
the waves and directs them into the ear. The
collected waves then travel through the ear
canal and reach the eardrum located in the
middle ear.

Sound is ⓐproduced through vibrations (A)[that /
what] occur from a sound source, when the strings
of a guitar (B)[is / are] played, for instance. The
vibrations of the sound source cause the air to
vibrate and the sound (C)[travelling / to travel] as
waves, similar to the ripples created in a lake when
you ⓑthrow a stone. When these sound waves
reach our ears, the brain interprets them as sound.
Just as different ripples in water might overlap if
you throw two stones, sound waves can also
interfere with each other when they ⓒmeet. There
are two types of interference: constructive and
destructive. Constructive interference occurs when
the ⓓpeaks of two waves overlap, resulting in a

solution: ⓓ taking → (to) take (help는 5형식 구문에서 목적격보어로 to부정사나 동사원형을 취하는 동사이므로, 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 동명사 taking을 동사원형인 take나 to부정사 to take로 고쳐야 한다. 그 외, 목 적어로 쓰인 명사 orders와 take를 수식하는 부사 accurately는 모두 알맞다.) ⓕ of → for (앞에 가주어 역할을 하는 it이 존재하며 이에 상응하는 진주어 인 to부정사구와 to부정사의 의미상 주어가 to부정사 앞에 쓰 이는 것은 알맞으나, to부정사의 의미상 주어는 ‘for＋목적격‘의 형태로 써야 하므로, of를 for로 고쳐야 한다. 참고로, nice, kind와 같이 사람의 성품을 나타내는 형용사가 앞에 올 때는 ‘of＋목적격‘의 형태로 나타낸다. 그 외, ‘~에 집중하다’라는 뜻 의 focus on이 쓰인 것과 on의 목적어로 동명사 driving이 이 어진 것은 모두 알맞다.)

Noise-cancelling technology is not only used in

this technology, such as ticket offices at tourist
attractions which are often very noisy. Microphones
ⓐare installed in ticket offices to detect external
noise, and an opposite sound wave is generated
and transmitted through a speaker, ⓑenabling the
ticket agent to hear the customer’s voice clearly.

패스트푸드 식당과 커피숍이다. They use noise-cancelling
headsets ⓒto improve communication between

These
noise-cancelling

help

audio
systems
generate
waves
to
cancel
out

solution: 관광지의 매표소에 마이크가 설치되어 외부 소음을 감지하고, 반대 음파를 생성하여 스피커를 통해 전송한다고 했으므로, ‘관광지의 매표소는 마이크를 사용해 외부 소음을 감지하고 제 거한다.’라고 설명한 Peter는 글의 내용을 잘 이해했다고 볼 수 있다. 또한, 노이즈 캔슬링 장치 덕분에 운전자가 산만한 소음 에 방해받지 않고 운전에 집중하는 것이 가능하다고 했으므로, ‘노이즈 캔슬링 기술로 인해 운전자들은 외부 소음에 방해받지 않고 운전에 집중할 수 있다.’라고 설명한 David 역시 글의 내 용을 잘 이해했다고 볼 수 있다. 미래엔(김성연) 3과 정답 본 콘텐츠는 해당 출판사로부터 교과서 라이센스를 획득하여 이그잼포유에서 제작하였습니다. 본 콘텐츠에 대한 저작권은 이그잼포유가 소유하고 있으며, 콘텐츠의 전부 또는 일부를 무단 전재하거나 배포하는 것은 저작권법에 의한 법적 책임 을 물을 수 있습니다. 본 콘텐츠의 레이아웃 및 편집에 대한 저작권 침해 행위 또한 금지하고 있습니다. 공통영어1 미래엔(김성연) 3과 예상문제 4회 - 객관식(선다형) 1. ③ 2. ①, ④ 3. 주관식 4. ⑤ 5. ④ 6. ⑤ 7. ② 8. ③ 9. ② 10. ④ 11. ③ 12. ⑤ 13. ③ 14. ④ 15. ⑤ 16. ③ 17. ④ 18. ⑤ 19. 주관식 20. ④ 정답 및 해설 ┃4회┃ 1) ③: ⓑ incredibly → incredible (주어인 단수대명사 That에 수일치 된 단수동사 sounds는 적절하나, ‘~인 것 같다’ 라는 뜻의 2형식 동사로 쓰인 sounds의 주격보어로 부 사는 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사 incredibly를 형용사인 incredible로 고쳐야 한다.) ⓒ did the self-cleaning system work → the self-cleaning system worked (전치사 about의 목적어로 간접의문문 이 올 수 있으나, 간접의문문은 ‘의문사(구)+평서문’의 어순이 되어야 하므로 의문부사 how에 이어지는 did the self-cleaning system work를 the self-cleaning system worked로 고쳐야 한다.) ⓔ can → could (wish의 목적어로 쓰인 명사절로, 내용 상 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황을 가정하고 있으므로, ‘주어+wish+(that+)주어+과거형 조동사+동사원형 ~’ 형 태의 가정법 과거 구문이 되도록 조동사 can을 과거형 인 could로 고쳐야 한다.) 오답 ⓐ 선행사 an amazing American woman을 수식하는 관계사절에서 선행사가 의미상 주어 역할을 하므로 주 격 관계대명사 who가 쓰이고, 선행사가 과거 특정 시기 (during the 1980s)에 ‘발명했던’ 주체이므로 능동태 과 거동사 invented와 목적어인 명사구 a self-cleaning house가 이어진 것은 모두 알맞다. ⓓ 앞서 언급된 내용을 가리키는 주어 역할의 지시대명 사 That이 쓰인 것과, 주어가 놀라움을 주는 주체에 해 당하므로 축약형으로 쓰인 is 뒤에 능동의 의미를 지닌 현재분사형 형용사 amazing이 주격보어로 쓰인 것은 알 맞다. ⓕ 조동사 would와 부정어구 never 뒤에 동사원형 have 가 쓰인 것과, ‘절대 ~할 필요가 없다’라는 뜻의 ‘never have+to부정사’ 구문이 되도록 have 뒤에 to부정사구인 to clean my room을 연결한 것은 모두 알맞다. 2) ①, ④ : Frances Gabe가 자동 청소 주택을 1980년대에 발명했다고 만 되어 있을 뿐 구체적인 연도에 대한 언급은 없으므로, ① ‘Frances Gabe는 몇 년도에 자동 청소 주택을 발명했는 가?’는 답할 수 없는 질문이다. 또한, 그녀가 실제로 그 집 에 살았다고 했을 뿐 그 기간에 대한 언급은 없으므로, ④ ‘Frances Gabe는 자동 청소 주택에 얼마나 오래 살았는 가?’도 답할 수 없는 질문이다. 오답 ② Frances Gabe는 어디 출신이었는가? (→ 미국) ③ 자동 청소 주택의 크기는 얼마나 되었는가? (→ 2층 높 이에 약 93m² 크기) ⑤ 연결된 관과 분사기는 집 전체에 무엇을 뿌렸는가? (→ 비눗물) 3) (1) which is (2) being used across various fields to reduce unwanted noise : (1) 쉼표 뒤에 noise-cancelling technology를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 써야 하므로, <조건>에 따라 noise-cancelling technology를 선행사로 하는 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대 명사 which를 쓰고, 단수인 선행사에 수일치 시킨 단수동 사 is를 쓴다. (2) 선행사인 noise-cancelling technology(노이즈 캔슬링 기술)가 ‘사용되고 있는’ 대상이며 진행 중인 일을 나타내 므로, 앞서 쓴 동사 is와 함께 ‘be동사+being+과거분사’ 구 조의 현재진행형 수동태를 이루도록 being used를 쓴다. 이어서 전치사 across와 목적어인 various fields를 쓴 뒤 <조건>에 제시된 to부정사가 오도록 목적을 나타내는 부 사적 용법의 to부정사 to reduce를 쓰고 이에 대한 목적어 로 unwanted noise를 연결한다. 4) ⑤: 상쇄 간섭은 한 파동의 마루가 다른 파동의 골과 겹쳐질 때 일어난다고 했으며, 뒤에는 더 작은 소리가 나거나 전혀 소리가 나지 않게 된다고 했으므로, 파동이 서로를 더 강화하는 것이 아니라 상쇄한다는 흐름이 되어야 한 다. 따라서 ‘strengthen(강화하다)’을 ‘cancel out(~을 상 쇄하다)’과 같은 표현으로 고쳐야 한다. 본문변형 cancel each other out → cancel out each other 오답 ⓐ 기타 줄이 연주될 때가 예시로 주어졌으므로, 소리가 음원에 발생하는 진동을 통해 생성된다는 흐름이 되는 ‘produced(생성되는)’는 적절하다. ⓑ 음원의 진동으로 공기가 진동하고 소리가 파도처럼 이동한다는 내용이 언급되므로, 이것을 돌을 던졌을 때 호수에 발생하는 잔물결에 빗대는 흐름이 되는 ‘throw (던지다)’는 적절하다. ⓒ 물에 두 개의 돌을 던지면 서로 다른 물결이 겹쳐질 수 있다는 내용이 언급되므로, 이와 비슷한 상황으로서 음파가 만나면 서로 간섭할 수 있다는 흐름이 되는 ‘meet(만나다)’는 적절하다. ⓓ 보강 간섭에 의해 파동이 더 커지고 소리가 더 커진 다고 했으므로, 보강 간섭이 두 파동의 마루가 겹쳐질 때 일어난다는 흐름이 되는 ‘peaks(마루들)’는 적절하다. 5) ④: (A) 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(occur from a sound source)이 이어지므로, 앞의 vibrations를 수식하는 관계 사절을 이루는 주격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다. 참고로, 공통영어1 미래엔(김성연) 3과 예상문제 4회 - 주관식(서답형) 3. (B) 부사절의 주어부(the strings of a guitar)에 이어진 술어동사 자리로, 주어의 핵인 the strings가 복수명사구 이므로, 복수동사인 are가 알맞다. (C) ’~가 …하도록 야기하다‘라는 뜻의 5형식 구문 ’cause+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)‘에서 ’목적어+목적 격보어‘인 the air to vibrate와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬연결되어 ’목적어+to부정사(구)‘ 구조를 이루어야 하 므로 목적어 the sound 다음의 목적격보어 자리에는 to 부정사인 to travel이 알맞다. 6) ⑤: 알맞다. 오답 ① 음악의 전체 볼륨을 증가시킨다 ② 음악의 소리를 더 명확한 품질로 향상시킨다 ③ 음악이 재생되지 않을 때 헤드폰을 조용하게 만든다 ④ 시끄러운 환경에서 음악 소리가 뭉개지게 만든다 7) ②: 관계대명사 that은 전치사 뒤에 올 수 없으므로 in which 를 in that으로 바꿀 수 없으며, 대신에 선행사 Another area에 어울리는 장소의 관계부사 where를 써서 ‘Another area where this technology is used’와 같이 전환할 수 있다. 오답 ① enabling 이하는 완전한 절에 쉼표로 연결되어 앞 절 의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문에 해당하므로, 흐름상 적 절한 접속사 and를 사용하고 앞 절 전체를 가리키는 대 명사 it과 이에 수일치된 단수동사 enables를 이용하여 전환한 것은 알맞다. ③ help는 5형식에서 목적격보어로 동사원형과 to부정사 를 모두 취할 수 있으므로, 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 동 사원형 take 대신에 to부정사인 to take를 사용하여 전 환한 것은 알맞다. ④ 쉼표 뒤에 쓰인 whose 이하는 선행사 cars를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절이므로 흐름상 적절한 접속사 and를 사용해 ‘접속사+주어+동사~’의 형태로 바 꾸어 쓸 수 있으며, 선행사 cars와 audio systems가 소유 관계이므로 ‘the+명사(구)+of+명사(구)’ 형태의 소유격 표현을 사용하여 ‘the audio systems of cars’로 전환한 것도 알맞다. ⑤ ‘가주어-진주어’ 구문에서 진주어 자리에는 to부정사 나 that절이 쓰일 수 있으며, 명사절 접속사 that 뒤에는 완전한 절이 와야 하므로, to부정사의 의미상 주어 for drivers를 that절의 주어 drivers로 바꾸고 to부정사 to focus를 동사 focus로 바꾸어 전환한 것은 알맞다. 8) ③: (A) 기술이 발전함에 따라 많은 사람들이 기대하는 것에 대한 내용에 해당하며, 소음 제거 기술이 원하지 않는 폐해를 줄여 문제를 해결하는 데 도움이 된다는 내용이 후반부에 언급되므로, 그것(기술)이 소음 공해로 인한 다 양한 사회적 문제들을 해결할 것이라고 기대한다는 흐름 이 되는 ‘solve(해결하다)’가 알맞다. exacerbate 악화시키다 (B) 소음 공해로 인한 다양한 사회적 문제들의 흔한 한 가지 원인이 시끄러운 이웃이라고 했으므로, 이에 대한 이유로서 이웃이 내는 소음이 주민들 간의 갈등으로 이 어질 수 있다는 흐름이 적절하다. 따라서 ‘conflict(갈등)’ 가 알맞다. harmony 조화 (C) 소음 제거 기술이 원하지 않는 폐해를 줄여 이러한 (소음으로 인한) 문제들을 해결하는 데 도움이 될 수 있 다고 했으므로, 이로써 사람들이 더 평화롭고 건강한 삶 을 살 수 있게 된다는 흐름이 적절하다. 따라서 ‘lead(살 아가다)’가 알맞다. long for ~을 갈구하다 본문변형 allowing people to lead → making people lead 9) ②: 어법상 어색한 것은 2개이다. ⓑ that → which (쉼표 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절 을 이끌어 선행사 the external part of the (→ 차량 소음을 제거함으로써 직원과 고객 사이의 의사소통을 향상시키기 위해 노이즈 캔슬링 헤드셋이 사용됨) Ben: 자동차의 오디오 시스템은 엔진과 도로 소리를 더 크게 만들어 운전자가 명확하게 들을 수 있도록 한다. (→ 노이즈 캔슬링 기술이 적용된 자동차의 오디오 시 스템은 엔진, 바람, 도로 소음과 같은 불쾌한 소음을 상 쇄하기 위해 파동을 발생시켜 운전자가 소음에 방해받 지 않고 운전에 집중할 수 있게 함)

G: Hey, look at the woman in this picture. It looks
like she’s making fun of someone.
B: I know, it does look like that, but she’s actually
just saying hi. In certain regions of Tibet, sticking
out tongues like that is a traditional way of
greeting people.
G: Really? So, it’s like waving our hands or giving a
high-five?
B: Yes, exactly! There’s an interesting history behind
why Tibetans do it.
G: Oh, yeah? What’s that?
B: Well, it’s said that there was a cold-blooded king
named Lang Darma, who had a black tongue. To
prove they weren’t related to him, Tibetans started
showing their tongues when they met someone new.
G: Oh, interesting. But isn’t sticking out tongues
considered a bit rude in some cultures, like ours?
B: That’s true, but not in Tibet. So, if you ever visit
Tibet, (A)make sure not to get offended when
someone sticks their tongue out at you!

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: be sure not to get offended
remember not to get offended
ensure that you don't get offended
be careful not to get offended
avoid not getting offended
solution: 밑줄 친 (A)는 ‘기분 나빠하지 마라’의 의미로, ‘~하지 않도록 조심해라’는 의미로 주의를 당부하는 표현인 ‘make sure not+to부정사’가 쓰였다. 그러나 ❺는 '기분이 상하지 않는 것 을 피하라‘의 의미로 이중 부정이 되어 다른 의미가 된다. 따 라서 avoid getting offended로 고쳐야 유사한 의미를 갖는다.

body:
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,
Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his
shaky hands. He chanted the names of the
ancestors, joining the past to the present once
more. The village went quiet and listened to his
chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our
genealogy, searching back across the centuries.
Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to
remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the
middle of the chant. The village waited in worried
silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most
of the whakapapa, but (A)그가 채워야 할 빠진 이름
들이 여전히 있었다. Now, he wanted me to drive
him to Murupara to finish his work.

choices: Honoring Nani’s Success
Echoes of Chanting by Ancestors
Nani’s Search for the Lost Village
Connecting the Past: Nani’s Mission
Lost Past and Halted Journey to the Past

body:
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather
most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing
names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to
drive him to Murupara to finish his work.
When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was shocked to
see how thin Nani Tama was. “Look, Nani,” I said.
“I’m not taking you anywhere. You could die on
me!” Nani looked at me in anger. “You want me to
die here in this room? Looking at these four walls?
When the whakapapa is (A)___________________?”
The old man held on tightly to the side of the
bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow,
painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could
not help but carry him to the car, and we set off
with Auntie.
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to
Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but
wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a
song that he had taught Auntie. They sang
together, lifting up their voices to send the song
flying like a bird through the sky.

choices: fully done
no longer needed

not yet finished
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

tattoos

life
experiences.

moko is less common these days, it is still

for the next generation.
(A)
(B)
(C)

Day?
B: World Bee Day? No, I haven’t. What’s that?
G: It’s a special day celebrated every year on May
20th. The United Nations created the day to
recognize the essential roles that bees play in
maintaining our ecosystem.
B: Oh, I had no idea there was such a day! But I
read somewhere that bees are endangered.
G: Unfortunately, that’s true. The decreasing number
of bees is a serious problem, especially because
about a third of the world’s food production
depends on them.
B: Oh, no! (A)I’m worried about what will happen if
the bee population continues to decrease.
G: Me, too. Let’s just hope that people become
more aware of the problem thanks to World Bee
Day.

I'm annoyed with

I feel uneasy about

cultural anthropologist. We often hear the phrase
“It’s a small world,” but is it really? Every culture
has its own unique traditions and customs, from
gestures to table manners. Something that looks
common to you might seem strange or unusual to
others. Let me give you some examples. In most
Western countries, it’s okay to open gifts right
away, but in China, it’s considered rude. Similarly,
touching a person’s head, including that of a child,
is impolite in Thailand and Laos, whereas it may be
no big deal in other countries. So it’s important to
___________________________________________________ when

citizen, make sure to acknowledge that each culture
has its own values that we should respect.

body:
For some time, my grandfather had been busy
writing down the village genealogy, known as the
whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old
house. But then came the night of the fire, which
ran through the house and destroyed our past. In
only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani
Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter,
my Auntie Hiraina.
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,
Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his
shaky hands. He chanted the names of the
ancestors, joining the past to the present once
more. The village went quiet and listened to his
chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our
genealogy, searching back across the centuries.
Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to
remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the
middle of the chant. The village waited in worried
silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most
of the whakapapa, but there were still missing
names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to
drive him to Murupara to finish his work.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: bringing peace to the family with chanting
overcoming Nani's despair through steady journaling
the challenges of rebuilding our lives after a big fire
restoring the whakapapa as a way to reconnectwith the past
Nani's hopelessness about failing to complete thewhakapapa

When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was shocked

said. “I’m not taking you anywhere. You could die
on me!” Nani looked at me in anger. “You want me

walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?”
The old man held on tightly to the side of the
bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow,
painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could
not help but ⓒto carry him to the car, and we set
off with Auntie.
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to
Nani chanting in the darkness. ⓓIt was strange but
wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a
song that he had taught Auntie. They sang
together, lifting up their voices to send the song
ⓔflying like a bird through the sky.

Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,
which has been a culturally significant practice of the
Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s
journey from their past to their present. (A) Each
curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a
person’s whakapapa(genealogy), social positions, and
personal accomplishments. (B) This explains why no
two tā moko designs look the same. (C) Traditionally,
the Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. (D) The permanence of facial tattoos makes
them a lifelong commitment, often leading to regret
or unforeseen consequences. (E) Men typically wear
tā moko over their entire faces, while women have
it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting
these designs in their teenage years, and as they
grow older, more lines and shapes are added to
their
tattoos
to
reflect
their
life
experiences.
Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a
rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā
moko is less common these days, it is still practiced
today by Maori people, who hope to preserve their
traditions and heritage for the next generation.

choices: Tā moko is the traditional tattoing art of Maori.
Tā moko represents the social status of the wearer.
No two Tā moko patterns are the same.
Only Maori men have Tā moko on their faces.
The Maori add more tattoos as they grow older.

전체가 그들의 과거를 복원했다 ⑤ 와카파파가 마침내 마땅한 주목을 받게 되었다 16) ④: 나니가 조상들의 이름을 읊조리며 과거와 현재를 다시 금 이어나갔고 마을은 조용히 그의 읊조림에 귀를 기 울였다고 묘사하고 있으므로 ④ ‘마을 사람들은 과거와 현재를 이어주는 나니의 읊조리는 소리를 들었다.’는 글 의 내용과 일치한다. 오답 ① 화재가 나기 전에, 나니는 마을 계보를 기록하느라 바쁘지 않았다(→ 바빴다). ② 나니는 그의 집을 파괴한 화재로부터 와카파파를 지켰다(→ 화재로 인해 와카파파를 잃었다). ③ 나니는 너무 절망적이어서 와카파파를 다시 쓰는 것조차 생각할 수 없었다. (→ 나니는 와카파파를 다시 쓰기 시작했다) ⑤ 마을 사람들의 걱정스러운 속삭임이 나니가 읊조리 는 것을 멈추게 했다. (→ 나니가 읊조리는 것을 멈추자 걱정스러운 침묵으로 기다렸다.) 17) ③: 타 모코 디자인이 개인의 계보, 사회적 지위와 개인적 성취를 보여주며, 나이가 들수록 삶의 경험을 나타내기 위해 더 많은 선과 모양을 문신에 더한다고 했으므로 타 모코가 과거에서 현재에 이르는 개인의 삶의 여정을 상징한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ③ ‘한 사람의 삶의 진행(과정)’가 가장 알맞다. 본문변형 an individual’s journey → the progression of one’s life 오답 ① 지도자들의 권위 ② 적들을 위협하는 한 방법 ④ 마오리족의 문화유산 ⑤ 그들이 믿는 초자연적인 힘 18) ③: (A) 문장의 동사가 없으므로, 동사가 와야 한다. Each ~ tā moko가 문장의 주어이며, of 앞의 ‘Each+단수명사 구‘에 수일치하므로 단수동사인 represents가 오는 것이 어법상 적절하다. (B) 등위접속사 and에 이어지는 두 번째 절로, 부사절 as ~ older에 대한 주절이 위치해야 한다. 뒤에 문장의 동사가 없으므로 동사의 위치이며, 주어 more lines and shapes가 ‘추가되는‘ 대상이므로 복수명사구에 수일치한 수동태 are added가 오는 것이 어법상 적절하다. (C) 콤마 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(hope ~ generation)을 이끌어, 사람을 가리키는 선행사 Maori people를 부연설명하고 있으므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 who가 알맞다. 참고로 that은 계속적 용법 에서 쓸 수 없다. 19) lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky : • ‘목소리를 높이면서’는 완전한 절 뒤에 오므로 분사구문 을 만들어야 하는데, 의미상 주어인 they가 ‘목소리를 높 이는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사를 사용하 여 lifting up their voices로 영작한다. • ‘노래를 날려 보내기 위해’는 동작의 목적(~하기 위해) 을 표현하는 부사적 용법의 to부정사를 이용하여 to send 를 쓰되, ‘~을 …하도록 보내다’를 뜻하는 5형식 ‘send+목 적어+목적격보어(현재분사)’ 구문을 사용하여, to send the song flying으로 영작한다. • ‘하늘을 가로지르는 새처럼‘은 두 개의 전치사구(‘하늘을 가로지르는’과 ‘새처럼’)로 이루어져 있으므로 ‘like a bird’ 와 ‘through the sky’를 붙여서 영작한다. 20) ⑤: ⓔ ‘미래를 위해 자원을 따로 모아 두다’의 영영풀이는 save가 ‘절약하다’의 의미로 쓰일 때의 풀이로 적절하다. 지문에 쓰인 saved는 ‘구했다’의 의미이므로 ‘to rescue someone or something from danger or harm(위험이 나 피해로부터 누군가 또는 어떤 것을 구해내다)’라는 영영풀이가 되어야 한다. 오답 ⓐ 응시하다: 눈을 깜빡이거나 돌리지 않고 오랫동안 무엇인가를 바라보다 ⓑ 친절한; 친절하고 차분하며, 누구나 어떤 것도 다치 거나 속상하지 않도록 조심하는 ⓒ 기억해내다, 상기하다: 과거의 어떤 일을 기억해 내다 ⓓ 속삭이다: 아주 작은 숨소리만 사용하여 부드럽게 말해, 소수의 사람만 들을 수 있도록 하다

presentation skills, such as using friendly gestures,
making natural eye contact, and (A)[speaks / speaking]
with an appropriate volume. But just as important,
well-designed slides play a critical role in effectively
conveying your message. Here are some useful tips
for improving your presentation slides. First, adopt a
“less is more” approach by keeping your slides simple.
Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases
instead of full sentences. This allows the audience to
focus more on listening than on reading. Next,
prioritize readability by carefully selecting attractive
font sizes and colors. The best readability is generally
(B)[achieved / achieving] with a font size of at least
18 pt, and you should limit slides to three or four
colors to avoid distraction. Lastly, enhance your slides
with high-quality images (C)[what / that] complement
the text. By following these simple tips, you can
create effective slides that hold your audience’s
interest and keep them engaged from start to finish!

It’s good to see you, everyone! I’m Dr. Edward
Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for
inviting me here today. On my way, I had trouble
locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came
up to me and walked me here. It’s fascinating how,
in situations like this, we want to help someone in
need. Now, this raises some interesting questions:
where does our friendliness come from, and why is
it important? To answer these questions, I’d like to
tell you about my childhood companion dog,
Sparky. When we played with a ball, I noticed that
he responded well to my gestures.

body:
How much of a coffee bean is used to make
coffee?
The world’s widespread love of coffee comes at a
substantial environmental cost, as the extraction
process generates significant waste. Only 0.2 percent
of a coffee bean is used to make coffee, with the
remaining 99.8 percent ⓐdisposing of as waste. As
a result, the vast quantity of coffee consumed
worldwide produces millions of tons of coffee waste
each year.
So, what happens to all the waste from the coffee
extraction process? Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are
classified as general waste and ⓑsent to landfills.
There they break down, releasing methane, a
greenhouse gas ⓒwhat is approximately 25 times
more potent than CO₂. Some SCGs are incinerated
instead of being buried, but this releases a lot of
CO₂: 338 kg per ton. (A)_______________, neither of
these waste management options takes into account
the potential value of coffee grounds. Although the
grounds contain valuable organic compounds and
minerals, they are simply destroyed.
(B)_______________, thanks to ⓓincreased awareness
of
the
coffee
waste
problem,
companies,
organizations, and governments around the world
ⓔare working hard to improve the environmental
impact of the coffee industry through circular
economy measures. A circular economy promotes
the reuse of resources for as long as possible,
reducing waste and environmental costs.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
choices: ThusUnluckily

HoweverFortunately

solution: (A) 커피박이 매립되어 메테인을 방출하거나 일부 다른 커피박 이 소각되어 많은 양의 이산화 탄소를 방출한다는 내용 다음 에, 이러한 쓰레기 관리 선택지 중 어느 것도 커피박의 잠재적 인 가치를 고려하지 않는다는 대조적인 내용이 이어지므로, However(하지만)가 알맞다. (B) 커피박이 가치 있는 유기 화합물과 무기질을 함유하고 있 음에도 그저 소실된다는 내용 다음에, 커피박 문제에 대한 높 아진 인식 덕분에 전 세계적으로 순환 경제 대책을 통해 커피 산업의 환경적 영향을 개선하려고 노력한다는 긍정적인 내용 이 이어지므로, Fortunately(다행히도)가 알맞다.

Did you know that you can grow tasty mushrooms
right in your home using spent coffee grounds?
Coffee grounds contain the perfect nutrients for
growing mushrooms. (A)여기 당신이 버섯 키우기를
시작하는 데 도움을 주는 단계별 안내가 있다. First,
mix 80 percent coffee grounds with 20 percent
mushroom spawn. Then, thoroughly wash a milk
container and make four small holes in the sides.
Fill the container about two-thirds full of the mixture
and close it tightly. Next, find a warm and dark
place with a temperature between 18 and 25˚C, and
place the container there for two to four weeks
until the mixture turns completely white. When this
happens, move the container to a bright area with
indirect sunlight and cut the top off. To keep the
mixture from drying out, spray it with water twice a
day. Within a week, you will notice tiny mushrooms
emerging. When the mushrooms grow tall, they are
ready to be picked. After that, you can enjoy your
mushrooms with your favorite dish!

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

The famous German musician Johann Sebastian
Bach once said, “Without my morning coffee, I’m
just like a dried-up piece of goat.” Today this
sentiment is shared by many, with coffee shops
springing up on almost every street corner, and it
is common to see city residents walking around
with a cup of coffee in hand. According to the
International
Coffee
Organization
(ICO),
approximately
10
million
tons
of
coffee
was
consumed worldwide between 2020 and 2021, and
Koreans made a significant contribution to this
huge total, consuming 150,780 tons of coffee. This
means that every Korean adult drank an average of
one cup of coffee every day throughout the year.
Clearly, for Koreans and other world citizens, coffee
is not just a drink but a daily necessity.

body:
An example of a circular economy in action occurs
when a chain of coffee shops (A)[collaborate /
collaborates] with an organization to collect spent
coffee grounds from its shops. These grounds are
processed to remove impurities and dried out. The
(B)[resulted / resulting] SCGs are sold to fertilizer
companies, where they are transformed into organic
fertilizer. This fertilizer is later sold back to the
coffee shop chain. The chain provides the fertilizer
to local eco-friendly farmers, (C)[who / that] then
sell their produce back to the chain. The farm
produce can be used to create various food items,
such as rice chips and dried sweet potatoes, which
are sold in the chain’s coffee shops. By repurposing
coffee grounds in this manner, related businesses
and local farmers can benefit both economically and
environmentally.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)         (C)
choices: collaborateresultedthat
collaboratesresultedwho
collaboratesresultingthat
collaborateresultingwho
collaboratesresultingwho
solution: (A) 주어부 a chain of coffee shops에 이어진 접속사 when의 부사절 동사 자리로, 주어부의 핵심 단어인 chain이 단수이므 로, 이에 수일치된 단수동사 collaborates가 알맞다. (C) 쉼표 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(then sell their produce back to the chain)을 이끌어 선행사 local eco-friendly farmers에 대해 부연 설명을 하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므 로, 주격 관계대명사 who가 알맞다. that은 계속적 용법으로 사용하지 않는다.

The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from
my hometown, Waituhi. “Can you take a week off?”
he asked. “Your Nani Tama wants you here.” “But
Dad!” I answered. “My boss won’t let me take any
more time off.” The phone went silent, and then I
heard my grandfather say faintly, “I need your help,
Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the
whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have
much time.” I just knew _______________________________
_______________________. “All right, Nani,” I replied with
a sigh. “I’ll come.”

body:
Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,
ⓐthat has been a culturally significant practice of
the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative ⓑand symbolic of an individual’s journey
from their past to their present. Each curved line
and pattern of tā moko represents a person’s
whakapapa(genealogy), social positions, and personal
accomplishments. This explains why no two tā
moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the
Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire
faces, while women have ⓒit on their lips and
chins. The Maori start getting these designs in their
teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines
and shapes are added to their tattoos ⓓto reflect
their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held
great importance as a rite of passage throughout
their lives. Although tā moko is less common these
days, it is still ⓔpracticed today by Maori people,
who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage
for the next generation.

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,
Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his
shaky hands.
(A) It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather
most of the whakapapa, but there were still
missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he
wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish
his work.
(B) He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining
the past to the present once more. The village
went quiet and listened to his chanting. His
voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy,
searching back across the centuries.
(C) Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult
to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped
in the middle of the chant. The village waited
in worried silence until the next name burst out
of his mouth.

When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was shocked to
see how (A)[fit / thin] Nani Tama was. “Look, Nani,” I
said. “I’m not taking you anywhere. You could die on
me!” Nani looked at me in (B)[anger / smile]. “You
want me to die here in this room? Looking at these
four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?”
The old man held on tightly to the side of the
bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow,
painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could
not help but carry him to the car, and we set off
with Auntie.
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to
Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but
wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he (C)[burst into
/ left out] a song that he had taught Auntie. They
sang together, lifting up their voices to send the
song flying like a bird through the sky.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)

fitsmileleft out

solution: (A) 나니의 모습을 보고 그의 여행을 말리고 있으므로 나니의 건 강 상태가 매우 안 좋았음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 나니 타마가 얼 마나 thin(말랐는지)를 보고 충격 받았다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. (B) 와카파파를 다 마치지도 못한 상태에서 가만히 앉아서 죽 음을 기다리는 대신 고통스럽고 힘들더라고 와카파파를 마무 리하러 가겠다는 강한 의지를 소리치며 보여주고 있으므로, 화 자가 그를 말렸을 때 분노의 감정을 느꼈다는 흐름이 자연스 럽다. 따라서 anger(화)가 난 상태로 화자에게 말했다는 표현이 오는 것이 알맞다. (C) 그가 딸에게 가르쳐준 노래였다고 하고 둘이 같이 목소리를 높여 불렀다는 내용이 이어지므로 나니가 딸에게 가르쳐줬던 노 래를 burst into(갑자기 불렀다)라는 표현이 흐름상 자연스럽다.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

For some time, my grandfather had been busy
writing down the village genealogy, known as the
whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old
house. But then came the night of the fire, which
ran through the house and destroyed our past. In
only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani
Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter,
my Auntie Hiraina.
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,
Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his
shaky hands. He chanted the names of the
ancestors, joining the past to the present once
more. The village went quiet and listened to his
chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our
genealogy, searching back across the centuries.
Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to
remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the
middle of the chant. The village waited in worried
silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most
of the whakapapa, but there were still missing
names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to
drive him to Murupara to finish his work.
choices: Nani kept the whakapapa in his old house.
The whakapapa was destroyed in a fire overnight.
Nani stayed with Hiraina after his house caughtfire.
Nani was able to remember some of the namesof his ancestors.
Sometimes Nani stopped his chanting to drawattention from the village.

Just before noon, we arrived at a small town
(A)[calling / called] Murupara. “Where do we go
now?” I asked Nani. He did not reply, but he was
searching inside himself, staring at the small houses.
Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After
turning the corner, we saw an old man (B)[to stand
/ standing] in front of a house. He welcomed Nani
Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the
message, “We must hurry.”
Now that day seems like a dream to me. I
remember the two old men sitting at the table and
the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked.
All through the quiet afternoon and into the
evening, they recalled missing names. I had a
strange feeling (C)[which / that] there were other
people in the room. I felt as if people from the
past were looking over the shoulders of the two
old men to see if the work was correct.
Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment
of silence,
the old man whispered
to Nani,
“Goodbye, friend.” Crying, they pressed their noses
together to say goodbye.

solution: (A) 완전한 절(we ~ town)에 이어져 앞의 명사구 a small town 을 수식하는 분사구로, 수식을 받는 명사구 a small town가 무 루파라라고 ‘불려지는’ 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분 사 called가 오는 것이 어법상 적절하다. (B) ‘…가 ~하는 것을 보다’의 의미로, ‘see+목적어+목적격보어 (동사원형/현재분사/과거분사)’의 구조로, 지각동사 saw와 목적 어 an old man 뒤에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리이다. 지각동사 의 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 때 목적격보어로 동사 원형 또는 진행을 강조하는 현재분사를, 목적어와 목적격보어 가 수동 관계일 때 과거분사를 사용하므로, 여기서는 an old man이 ‘서있는‘ 주체이자 진행을 강조하는 현재분사 standing 이 오는 것이 어법상 적절하다. It was early morning and still dark when we
returned to Auntie’s place. All the lights were on,
and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling,
Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it
to the village. Our hearts were full because our
grandfather had saved our past for us. Our Nani
Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired. He sighed.
“At last, I may go now.” Then, he closed his eyes.
“No, Dad!” Auntie Hiraina cried. The sun burst
across the hills.

solution: 완성된 와카파파를 마을 사람들에게 건넨 뒤 눈을 감은 나니 타마의 마지막을 묘사하는 글이므로 글의 제목으로 ❶ ‘나니 타마의 마지막 선물’이 가장 적절하다. ② 우리의 과거의 마지막 숨결 ③ 잃어버린 고향으로의 귀환 ④ 우리의 과거와 끊어진 연결 ⑤ 마을 사람들과의 마지막 재회 미래엔(김성연) 2과 정답 본 콘텐츠는 해당 출판사로부터 교과서 라이센스를 획득하여 이그잼포유에서 제작하였습니다. 본 콘텐츠에 대한 저작권은 이그잼포유가 소유하고 있으며, 콘텐츠의 전부 또는 일부를 무단 전재하거나 배포하는 것은 저작권법에 의한 법적 책임 을 물을 수 있습니다. 본 콘텐츠의 레이아웃 및 편집에 대한 저작권 침해 행위 또한 금지하고 있습니다. 공통영어1 미래엔(김성연) 2과 예상문제 3회 - 객관식(선다형) 1. ③ 2. ① 3. ① 4. 주관식 5. ②, ④ 6. 주관식 7. 주관식 8. 주관식 9. ①, ② 10. 주관식 11. ③ 12. ④ 13. ③ 14. ⑤ 15. ③ 16. 주관식 17. ① 18. ⑤ 19. ② 20. ① 정답 및 해설 ┃3회┃ 1) ③: ⓒ they는 시들을 가리키고 메시지를 이해하기 위해 추 론해야(행간 사이를 읽어야) 하며 이해하기 힘들다고 설 명하므로 시들이 clear(명확한)하다는 표현은 어색하다. 대신 ambiguous(모호한) 또는 unclear(분명하지 않은)의 표현이 오는 것이 알맞다. *본문에는 unclear가 쓰임 오답 ⓐ 유민이는 시의 모호성이 시를 아름답게 만든다고 생 각한다고 말하고 있으며, Brent가 유민이 시 읽기를 정 말로 사랑하는 것 같다고 언급되었으므로, 유민이는 시 에 interested(관심 있는) 상태라는 표현은 알맞다. ⓑ 시보다는 소설을 더 선호한다고 했으므로 Brent에게 시가 약간 boring(지루한) 것으로 생각된다는 흐름은 자 연스럽다. ⓓ 시를 해석하는 데 있어 정답이 없다고 설명하고 있으 므로 누구든지 시를 differently(다르게) 해석할 수 있다 는 표현은 자연스럽다. ⓔ Brent가 시 읽기를 시도해보겠다고 한 말에 유민이 시 낭독회에 Brent를 초대하여 그가 가겠다고 대답하므 로 낭독회에 가서 시를 자연스럽게 접하고 좋은 시들을 만나게 될 것이므로 이는 시를 appreciating(감상하기) 시작할 좋은 기회라는 흐름은 자연스럽다. 2) ①: 유민이 수업 시간에 배운 시를 이해하려고 하고 있다고 설명하고 있으므로 ① ‘유민이 수업에서 공부한 소설을 공부하고 있다.’는 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. 오답 ② 유민과 달리, Brent는 소설을 시보다 더 좋아한다. ③ 유민은 시와 소설이 공통점이 있다고 생각한다. ④ Brent는 시에서 숨겨진 메시지를 해석하는 것이 어렵 다고 느낀다. ⑤ 유민과 Brent는 토요일에 함께 시 낭독 행사에 갈 것 이다. 3) ①: 처음엔 휴가를 더 이상 내기 힘들다고 거절하던 화자가 할아버지의 간곡한 부탁으로 결국 가겠다고 대답하고 있 으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 표현은 어쩔 수 없이 가기로 결심 했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ① ‘나는 선택의 여지가 없었다’가 가장 알맞다. 오답 ② 그가 나에게 거짓말을 했다 ③ 나는 그를 위해 시간을 더 벌어야 했다 ④ 나는 그에게 내 상황을 말해야 했다 ⑤ 그것이 그가 원하는 것인지 확실히 해야 했다 4) (1) allow him to take any more time off (2) drive, complete the whakapapa 질문 (1) 화자는 아버지의 요청을 왜 거절했나? → 그의 상사가 그가 더 이상 휴가를 내는 것을 허락하지 않을 것이라 생각했기 때문이다. (2) 나니는 그의 손자에게 무엇을 하도록 요청했나? → 그는 와카파파를 완성할 수 있도록 손자가 그를 무루파 라로 운전해 줄 것을 요청했다. 5) ②, ④ : ⓑ when → which (콤마 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 문 장을 이끌어 the fire를 부연 설명하고 있으므로, 완전한 문장과 함께 쓰이는 관계부사 when은 올 수 없으며, when을 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which로 고쳐 써 야 한다.) ⓓ for Nani Tama → Nani Tama (‘(사람)이 ~하는데 (시간) 이 걸린다’는 ‘it+take+사람+시간+to부정사’ 또는 ‘it takes+ 시간+for+사람+to부정사’로 표현하는데, 여기서 시간에 해 다하는 almost two years가 간접목적어로 뒤에 쓰였으므로 for을 삭제하고 직접목적어 Nani Tama로 고쳐야 한다. 오답 ⓐ 콤마 뒤에 ‘관계대명사+be동사‘인 which was가 생략되 어 있는 분사구로, 부연 설명하는 the village genealogy는 와카파파로 ’알려진‘ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거 분사 known(알려진)의 쓰임은 어법상 알맞다. ⓒ lines를 수식하고 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장을 이끌고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 that의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. ⓔ ‘~이 있다’는 의미의 ‘there+be동사’는 동사 뒤에 주어 가 오고 be동사는 주어의 수와 일치시키므로 복수주어인 missing names와 수일치시킨 복수동사 were의 쓰임은 어 법상 적절하다. 6) everything we knew was gone. : • ‘모든 것이 사라졌다’는 everything was gone으로 영작할 수 있다. • ‘우리가 알았던’은 everything을 수식하는 형용사절이므로 관계대명사 that 뒤에 we knew를 쓰고 선행사인 everything 바로 뒤에 이어 쓰는데 총 5단어로 영작하라는 조건이 있으므로 목적격 관계대명사 that을 생략시켜 everything we knew was gone으로 영작을 완성한다. 공통영어1 미래엔(김성연) 2과 예상문제 3회 - 주관식(서답형) 4. 있으므로, 분사구문 이 오는 자리이다. 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어 인 he이며 ‘응시하는’ 주체이므로 stared를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사인 staring으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ 접속사가 남아있는 분사구문으로, 의미상 주어인 주절의 주어 we가 길모퉁이를 ‘돈‘ 주체이므로, 과거분사 turned를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사인 turning으로 고쳐야 한다. 또는 전치사 after 뒤에 이어지는 목적어로 볼 수도 있는데, 전치사 뒤에 동사가 올 수 없으므로, turned를 동명사 turning으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ 구접속사 as if[as though](마치 ~처럼)는 추측하거나 실제와는 다른 것을 가정하는 표현으로, 사실일 수 있는 추측의 경우 직설법으로 쓰지만, 가정의 경우 주절과 같은 시제이면 가정법 과거로 ‘were/과거형’을 쓰고, 주절보다 이전 시제이면 가정법 과거완료 ‘had p.p.’를 쓴다. 본문에 서는 주절 동사 felt의 과거시제와 같은 시제로, 과거에서 온 사람들이 실제로는 없지만 마치 보고 있는 것처럼 가 정하고 있으므로, 가정법 과거완료인 had been은 가정법 과거 were로 고쳐야 한다. 오답 ⓐ 완전한 절 we ~ town 뒤에서 a small town을 수식하 고 있으므로 분사구문이 오는 자리인데 행위의 주체인 a small town은 무루파라라고 불렸으므로 수동의 의미를 갖 는 과거분사 called의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. ⓓ ‘~이 있다’라는 뜻의 there + be 동사는 동사 뒤에 쓰 인 주어의 수와 일치시키므로 복수명사인 other people과 수일치 시킨 복수동사 were의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. ⓕ 완전한 절 they ~ together 뒤에 놓이고 주절 동작의 목적(작별 인사를 하기 위해)을 나타내므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사(~하기 위해)인 to say의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. 8) old men, missing names, done 요약문 두 노인이 빠져있던 이름들을 되찾기 위해 조용한 마을에서 재회했고 그들의 작업은 마침내 끝났다. 9) ①, ② : ⓐ 콤마 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(has ~ years)을 이끌어 Tā moko를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사 절이므로, 계속적 용법에는 쓸 수 없는 that을 계속적 용 법의 주격 관계대명사 which로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ ‘A 뿐만 아니라 B도‘를 뜻하는 표현으로 not only A but also B가 짝지어 쓰이므로 and을 but also로 고쳐야 한다. 오답 ⓒ 타 모코를 지칭하는 목적격 대명사가 오는 자리이므로 단수 대명사인 it의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. ⓓ 완전한 절 뒤에 오고 주절의 동작의 목적을 나타내므 로 ’~하기 위하여‘라는 의미를 갖는 부사적 용법의 to부정 사 to reflect의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. ⓔ 주어 it은 타 모코를 지칭하고 이는 ’실행되는‘ 대상이 므로 수동태로 표현되어야 한다. 따라서 be 동사인 is 뒤 에 과거분사인 practiced의 쓰임은 어법상 적절하다. 10) tattooing, individual’s journey, curved lines 제시문 구부러진 선과 패턴을 가진 개인의 여정에 대한 상 징적 표현인 마오리족의 문신, 타 모코 11) ③: 과거의 잿더미에서 벗어날 방법을 찾기 위해 나니가 다 시 와카파파를 기록하기 시작했다는 주어진 글에 이어, He가 나니를 지칭하고 그가 조상들의 이름들을 읊조렸 고 그의 목소리에 마을 사람들이 귀를 기울였다는 내용 의 (B), 기억해 내기 어려운 부분에 그가 읊조림을 멈추 면 마을 사람들도 걱정스레 침묵하며 다음 이름이 나오 기를 기다렸다는 (C), 그러한 작업이 거의 2년에 이어졌 지만 여전히 빠진 이름들이 있어 그의 작업을 마무리하 려고 무루파라로 가려한다는 내용의 (A)로 이어지는 것 이 알맞다. 12) ④: (A) 나니의 모습을 보고 그의 여행을 말리고 있으므로 나니의 건강 상태가 매우 안 좋았음을 알 수 있다. 따 라서 나니 타마가 얼마나 thin(말랐는지)를 보고 충격 받았다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. fit (몸이) 건강한, 탄탄한 (B) 와카파파를 다 마치지도 못한 상태에서 가만히 앉아 서 죽음을 기다리는 대신 고통스럽고 힘들더라고 와카 파파를 마무리하러 가겠다는 강한 의지를 소리치며 보 여주고 있으므로, 화자가 그를 말렸을 때 분노의 감정을 느꼈다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 anger(화)가 난 상 태로 화자에게 말했다는 표현이 오는 것이 알맞다. smile 미소 (C) 그가 딸에게 가르쳐준 노래였다고 하고 둘이 같이 목소리를 높여 불렀다는 내용이 이어지므로 나니가 딸 에게 가르쳐줬던 노래를 burst into(갑자기 불렀다)라는 표현이 흐름상 자연스럽다. leave ~ out ~을 배제하다, 생략하다, 무시하다 13) ③: 어둠 속에서 여행하면서 나니가 읊조리는 소리를 듣는 것이 낯설지만 아름다웠다고 했으므로 ③ ‘어둠 속 에 서 나니의 읊조림을 들으면서 밤새 여행하는 것은 화 자를 겁먹게 했다.’는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. 오답 ① 화자는 나니가 여행하기에 너무 약해 보였기 때문 에 그를 데려가고 싶지 않았다. ② 나니는 와카파파를 완성하지 않은 채 죽고 싶지 않 았다. ④ 나니는 그가 걸을 수 있다는 것을 증명하기 위해 최선을 다했다. ⑤ 고모는 나니에게서 그 노래를 배웠기 때문에 그와 함께 노래 부를 수 있었다. 14) ⑤: 기억해 내기 어려운 부분에서 갑자기 읊조림을 멈추었 고 마을 사람들이 걱정스러운 침묵 속에서 다음 이름 이 터져 나오기를 기다렸다고 묘사하고 있으므로 ⑤ ‘가끔 나니는 마을 사람들의 주의를 끌기 위해 그의 읊 조림을 멈췄다.’는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. 오답 ① 나니는 와카파파를 그의 옛집에 보관했다. ② 와카파파는 하룻밤 사이에 불에 타서 파괴되었다. ③ 나니는 그의 집이 불타고 난 후 히라이나와 함께 지냈다. ④ 나니는 그의 조상들의 몇몇 이름을 기억해 낼 수 있었다. 15) ③: (A) 완전한 절(we ~ town)에 이어져 앞의 Sound is produced through vibrations that occur
from a sound source, when the strings of a guitar
are played, for instance. The vibrations of the sound
source cause the air to vibrate and the sound to
travel as waves, similar to the ripples created in a
lake when you throw a stone. When these sound

peaks of two waves overlap, resulting in a bigger
wave and a louder sound. Destructive interference,

overlaps with a valley of another wave, so they
cancel each other out and produce a quieter sound,

Have you ever wondered what happens to sound
waves when they enter our ears? Let’s take a closer
look. The journey starts from the external part of
the outer ear, (A)[that / which] gathers the waves
and directs them into the ear. The collected waves
then travel through the ear canal and reach the
eardrum located in the middle ear. When the
eardrum vibrates, these vibrations (B)[transmit / are
transmitted] to three small bones in the middle ear.
These bones make the vibrations stronger and then
pass them to a snail-shaped structure in the inner
ear. Inside this fluid-filled structure are tiny hair
cells. When the vibrations make waves in the fluid,
the tiny hair cells move and generate electrical
signals that travel to the auditory nerve. This nerve
carries the information to the brain, where the
signals are interpreted, allowing us (C)[hear / to
hear] sound. Undoubtedly, it is a quite remarkable
journey!

cancel each other out and produce a quieter sound,

body:
Have you ever wondered what happens to sound
waves when ⓐthey enter our ears? Let’s take a
closer look. The journey starts from the external
part of the outer ear, which gathers the waves and
directs them into the ear. The collected waves then
travel through the ear canal and reach the eardrum
located in the middle ear. When the eardrum
vibrates, these vibrations are transmitted to three
small bones in the middle ear. These bones make
the vibrations stronger and then pass ⓑthem to a
snail-shaped structure in the inner ear. Inside this
fluid-filled structure are tiny hair cells. When the
vibrations make waves in the fluid, the tiny hair
cells move and generate electrical signals that travel
to the auditory nerve. This nerve carries the
information to the brain, where the signals are
interpreted, allowing us to hear sound. Undoubtedly,
it is a quite remarkable journey!

art, despite ⓐchallenges in their lives. Each artist
has a unique painting style and story that has
made their work highly valued. Let’s explore each
artist’s life and artwork.
Bill Traylor
The first artist we’re going to examine (A)[are / is]
Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S.
in 1853 and spent his early life working on a
cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free
man after the American Civil War, he still had to
face racial discrimination, working for very ⓑlow
wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70
years
old,
Traylor
moved
to
the
city
of
Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a
factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and
became too ill to work (B)[what / that] he ⓒturned
away from drawing to express his life experiences.
Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings,
starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog.
Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had
often been used on farms to watch and hunt
slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in
these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and
Man with Umbrella portrays the ⓓfree lives of
African Americans that he observed on the streets
of Montgomery. (C)[Used / Using] simple shapes
and colors, Traylor ⓔcaptured complex moments in
American history from slavery to freedom. As a

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may
have encountered docents and curators. While these
two roles may appear similar, they actually have
quite different responsibilities, requiring different
skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin
word meaning “to teach,” docents are guides who
lead museum tours and provide information about
the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition.
They are usually volunteers who have a passion for
art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out
their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized
training in presentation and communication skills.
On the other hand, curators are professionals who
design and organize exhibitions, with the word
curator coming from a Latin word meaning “to take
care of.” Curators determine the main theme of
each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the
theme, and arrange them in an engaging way
which captivates the audience. Curators are typically
employed by museums and are expected to possess
advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or
a related field. Despite _______________________________,
both docents and curators share a common goal:
enriching every visitor’s experience.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

their academic knowledge
their social prestige
their inherent gift
their distinct roles

Maud Lewis
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist
known for her ⓐheart-warming paintings. Born in a
small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from
physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and
fingers. This ⓑrestricted her mobility and caused
her to drop out of school. To make a living, she
began to paint and sell Christmas cards. (A) When
her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with
her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her
future
husband,
Everett
Lewis.
(B)
She
often
depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as

mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple
forms, ⓒgenerating an original, innovative style. (D)
Although her physical limitations confined her to a
small cottage, her talent and imagination were both
limitless. (E) In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear
on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen
shows decorated cows standing in a flower field.
With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a
ⓓmagical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her
paintings gradually ⓔlost popularity, her story
inspired many people and was later made into
books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love
for the world through her paintings and became an
iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

body:
Anna Ancher
Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this
exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from
Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may
notice a common theme — they all feature female
figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later
moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting
school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris,
(A)[which / in which] was unusual for women at the
time. Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she
was able to take advantage of these opportunities.
Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in
painting, (B)[objecting / objected] to the social
pressure that married women were to solely focus
on household duties. Ancher differed from other
artists of that era, who depicted women as still life
subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active
participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works
The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s
Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color,
which (C)[contributing / contributed] to the rich
Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting
Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the
sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed.
Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women
in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional
artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us
to this day.

(B)
(C)

skillfully explored light and color, ⓓcontributing to
the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her
painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection
of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly
portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles
of women in the 20th century and displayed her
exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to
amaze us to this day.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

Bill Traylor
The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill
Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in
1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton
farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man
after the American Civil War, he still had to face
racial discrimination, working for very low wages on
the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old,
Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama,
where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until
he was 85 years old and became too ill to work
that he turned to drawing to express his life
experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of
his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and
Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs
because they had often been used on farms to
watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is
expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast,
Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays
the free lives of African Americans that he observed
on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes
and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in
American history from slavery to freedom. As a
result, he’s now considered an important figure in
American folk art.
Bill Traylor, who was born into slavery and
(A)____________ racial discrimination throughout his
life, began painting to express his experiences and
captured complicated moments in American history
using simple shapes and colors, which made him
a(n) (B)____________ artist in American folk art.
(A)
(B)

다음 글의 Maud Lewis에 관한 내용과 일치하지않는 것은?

Maud Lewis
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known
for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small
Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical
weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers.
This limited her mobility and caused her to drop
out of school. To make a living, she began to paint
and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed
away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby,
Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband,
Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the
rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to
paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in
paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her
artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil
paints and simple forms, generating an original,
innovative style. Although her physical limitations
confined her to a small cottage, her talent and
imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red
maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape,
and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in
a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings
create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As
her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story
inspired many people and was later made into
books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love
for the world through her paintings and became an
iconic figure in Canadian folk art.
choices: Her physical weaknesses restricted her movement,which forced her to leave school.
She met Everett Lewis after moving to Digby,Nova Scotia, and spent the rest of her life withhim there.
She used bright colors and simple shapes tocreate a distinctive style, thanks to talent andimagination undiminished by her physical limits.
Her works Red Sleigh and A Pair of Oxen realisticallydepicted nature and animals as they are.
Through her paintings, she showed her love for theworld and became a symbol of Canadian folk art.

AI-powered
neural
implants,
(A)their
amazing

ⓓstimulate targeted regions of the brain at the right

Neuroscience has a long history of exploring
treatments for disorders of the nervous system,
including the brain and spinal cord. Traditionally,
researchers have studied various functions of neural
implants, which are medical devices like computer
chips that can be implanted in the nervous system.

for the future, and the ethical concerns surrounding
them.
First, let’s explore how this fascinating technology
has been applied. The AI-powered neural implant
(A)_______________________________________________________.
For instance, neural implants are used to treat brain
disorders like Parkinson’s disease. These implants
electrically stimulate targeted regions of the brain at
the right time with the help of AI to restore normal
brain activity. In addition, paralyzed people can
have the ability to walk again with the help of a
“digital bridge” between two implants inserted into
their brain and spine. When they think about
moving their legs, the AI analyzes the brain signals
and sends them to their legs through the implants.

artificial arms operated by the same mechanism.

began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her
parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her
aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her
future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the
couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis
continued to paint. She often ⓑdepicted the Digby
landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby
Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and
vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an
ⓒoriginal, innovative style. Although her physical
limitations ⓓconfined her to a small cottage, her
talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red
Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter
landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows
standing in a flower field. With these features,
Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of
a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained
popularity, her story inspired many people and was
later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis
expressed her love for the world through her
paintings
and
became
an

figure

notice a ⓐcommon theme — they all feature female
figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later
moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting
school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris,
which was ⓑunusual for women at the time.

able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even
after getting married, Ancher ⓒpersisted in painting,
objecting to the social pressure that married women
were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher
ⓓfollowed other artists of that era, who depicted

tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen

users.
A widely used dark pattern is the practice of

membership fee after a free trial ends. Companies

seeing a message such as “Hurry! One item left!”
even though you didn’t intend to buy it? Or have
you ever felt rushed into making a purchase
because of a limited-time offer? If you have, then
you ⓐmay have fallen prey to a dark pattern. Dark
patterns are manipulative designs on websites and
applications that trick users into making unintended
decisions. These deceptive practices often have
consequences that cause financial damages to the
users.
A widely used dark pattern is the practice of
“forced continuity,” which requires users to pay a
membership fee after a free trial ends. Companies
deliberately avoid informing users about the end of
the free trial period or make the cancellation
process ⓑcomplicate. (A)_____________, users have to
pay membership fees even if they no longer want
to use the service.
Another common type of dark pattern is known as
“hidden fees.” This design suddenly adds extra fees
at the last step of the ordering process. On the
final page, consumers are surprised to discover
additional charges, such as shipping or processing
fees, which the seller ⓒhas added to increase the
final cost of the order.
“Confirm-shaming” is another online trick ⓓthat
users
should
be
aware
of.
This
technique
manipulates users into feeling ashamed for cancelling
their membership or requesting a refund for an
order. Companies use this to keep their members
ⓔsubscribed, even if it goes against the members’
intentions. (B)____________, when users want to cancel
their subscription, they are offered two options: “I
want to keep my benefits” and “I want to give up
my benefits.” The first option is presented in an
appealing way, while the second option seems like
a bad choice.

How is the first option presented compared tothe second option in subscription cancellation?

physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and

create a magical quality, like (C)[that / those] of a fairy

love for the world through her paintings and
became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

Anna Ancher
Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this
exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from
Denmark. When ⓐobserving her paintings, you may
notice a common theme — they all feature female
figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later
moved to Copenhagen ⓑto attend a private
painting school. After that, she even studied abroad
in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time.
Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she was
able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even
after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting,
objecting to the social pressure that married women
were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher
differed from other artists of that era, ⓒwhich
depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast,
she showcased them as active participants in
everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in
the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also
skillfully explored light and color, ⓓcontributing to

portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles
of women in the 20th century and displayed her

ⓔexploring the exhibition.

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may
have encountered docents and curators. While these
two roles may appear similar, they actually have
quite different responsibilities, requiring different
skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin
word meaning “to teach,” docents are guides who
lead museum tours and provide information about
the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition.
They are usually volunteers who have a passion for
art and enjoy (A)[sharing / questioning] their
knowledge.
To
carry
out
their
responsibilities
effectively, docents need specialized training in
presentation and communication skills. On the other
hand, curators are professionals who design and
organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming
from a Latin word meaning “to take care of.”
Curators
determine
the
main
theme
of
each
exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme,
and arrange them in an engaging way which
(B)[captivates / distracts] the audience. Curators are
typically employed by museums and are expected
to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum
studies, or a related field. Despite their (C)[distinct /
similar] roles, both docents and curators share a
common goal: enriching every visitor’s experience.

(A)
(B)
(C)

questioningdistractssimilar

These two baby bears were rescued after they
(A)[have / had] been raised illegally in a tiny cage on
a farm for many years. To help the bears restore their
natural instincts, we carried out some special activities
(B)[knowing / known] as “behavioral enrichment.” For
example, we made honey-log feeders for the bears.
First, we made several holes in a log and filled them
with honey. Then, we hung the honey-log feeders on
trees near the bears’ habitat. As bears are intelligent
and curious creatures, they can become bored and
stressed when (C)[lacking / lacked] mental and

때만큼 활발한 상태를 유지하도록 해준다. After a while,
Ben and Lily approached the feeders and started
eating the honey inside. They are so cute!

elephant. After spending 25 years carrying tourists
along rough roads, she developed a twisted spine
and foot pain. In order to support Jane in taking

G: Hello, everyone! I’m Kelly. Are you thinking of
adopting a hamster? Today, I’d like to share
what I’ve learned from raising my hamster. First
of all, it’s important to understand that hamsters
are quite sensitive. While many people think that
taking care of hamsters is easy, they actually
require a lot of special attention. For example,
hamsters are active at night and sleep during
the day, so it’s crucial to provide a quiet
environment during the day. Also, their living
areas need to be cleaned regularly, and they
should be provided with fresh food and water
every day. One final tip: hamsters have poor
vision but have a strong sense of hearing. So,
try to spend some time talking to them near
their cage, and you’ll be amazed at how they
recognize your voice and respond to it. Keep
these tips in mind and take responsibility for
your hamster’s care.

Let Bears Bear the Right to Live Freely
Bears are a fascinating group of animals with eight
species, all living in very different habitats around
the world. Polar bears, for example, (A)[live / living]
in the Arctic, whereas Andean bears live in South
America. These bears should have the freedom to
live, but they are often killed when they come into
contact with humans. One of the worst examples of
this is bear bile farming. Brown bears in Eurasia and
North America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia, and
Asiatic black bears in Asia are often hunted and kept
illegally for their bile, which (B)[is / are] sold at a
high price for traditional Asian medicine. Although
bile farming is prohibited in many countries, it
continues due to the constant demand. Governments
and animal welfare organizations make persistent
attempts to find these farms and rescue the bears,
allowing them (C)[live / to live] in bear sanctuaries or
other safe places. Since UNESCO stated in 1978 that
animals are born with the right to be respected,
progress has been made in animal rights. However,
some animals are still not fully protected outside the
law, and need more of our attention and care.
(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: live arelive
live islive
living areto live
live isto live

July 31, Wednesday
This morning, we had the opportunity to learn
about animal treatment thanks to Molly, an elderly
elephant. After spending 25 years carrying tourists
along rough roads, she developed a twisted spine
and foot pain. In order to support Jane in taking
care of Molly’s foot, we took part in positive
reinforcement training, which _________________________
_________________________________________. When I gently
touched her foot with a pole and called out, “foot,”

piece of watermelon, her favorite fruit. This training
helps reduce the stress that animals experience
during controlled situations, such as treatment or a
health examination. The good news is Molly seems
to be adapting well, and I expect her to get better
soon.

seeing a message such as “Hurry! One item left!”
even though you didn’t intend to buy it? Or have
you ever felt rushed into making a purchase

the cancellation process complicated. As a result,

dark pattern. Dark patterns are manipulative
designs on websites and applications that trick
users into making unintended decisions.

that cause financial damages to the users. A
widely used dark pattern is the practice of
“forced continuity,” which requires users to pay
a membership fee after a free trial ends.
